options.label_head: FNA smear only — ADEQUATE, and the cytology reports a neoplastic / mal
options.rationale: Smear-only tier: needs the Cytology document, no tissue or cell block (Histology) and no flow (Lab Report); IHC beside Cytology is immunocytochemistry and stays at this tier.

options.rationale: Sibling of option 1 that differs only by the cytological reading (benign picture), which no document expresses, so it fits the same sets.

options.label_head: FNA smear only — INADEQUATE / non-diagnostic ("too few cells for cytol
options.rationale: Inadequate aspirate is an outcome state of the specimen, not a document set.

options.label_head: FNA smear only — technically UNINTERPRETABLE (air-dried, obscured by b
options.rationale: Technically uninterpretable aspirate is an outcome state of the specimen, not a document set.

options.label_head: FNA + cell block, or core needle biopsy, or excisional / incisional bi
options.rationale: Tissue or cell-block report with no IHC and no flow: requires Histology and excludes IHC and Lab Report; genetics alone does not lift it.

options.label_head: Tissue (cell block / core / excisional) WITH immunohistochemistry and/
options.rationale: Tissue with IHC and/or flow: requires Histology plus an IHC Report or a Lab Report read as flow; excludes genetics so option 8 holds the higher rung.

options.label_head: Effusion, CSF, marrow aspirate or node aspirate WITH flow cytometry —
options.rationale: Fluid or aspirate cytology with flow cytometry and no tissue block: requires Cytology and a Lab Report read as flow, and excludes Histology.

options.label_head: Tissue with IHC/flow PLUS cytogenetics / FISH, or plus molecular / NGS
options.rationale: Cumulative rung: tissue, IHC and/or flow, and a gene report; histology plus genetics without IHC or flow falls to option 5.

options.label_head: Malignancy excluded on review — reactive, infective or non-neoplastic;
options.rationale: Malignancy excluded on review is a conclusion that does not follow from which documents exist.

nodes.question_edit: What reports are in this patient's file?

options.label_head: Referral or clinical note only — no pathology report in the file
options.rationale: Lowest tier. Fits every set with neither a Histology Report nor a Cytology document, so lab, imaging, IHC or gene reports on their own fall here and understate.

options.label_head: Morphology only — skin biopsy, marrow biopsy and/or a blood or marrow
options.rationale: Morphology (biopsy or smear) with no IHC Report. A lab or gene report beside morphology without IHC falls here and understates.

options.label_head: Morphology + IHC (tryptase, CD117, and/or CD25 / CD30 / CD2)
options.rationale: Judged: option 3 is a cumulative rung above this one, so the two must not fit the same set; a clerk should not be asked to choose between a tier and the tier that strictly contains it. Excluding the Lab Report makes option 3 exclusive. Sets with a gene report but no Lab Report stay here, which understates the KIT result.

options.label_head: Morphology + IHC + basal serum tryptase and/or KIT molecular result
options.rationale: Judged: the rung needs morphology, IHC and a tryptase or KIT result. The schema allows one any_of group, which is spent on morphology, so the Lab Report (basal serum tryptase) is required and the gene report (KIT) cannot be an alternative. A KIT-only file falls to option 2, which understates and is the safe direction. Proposer A's alternative (require Histology, any_of lab or genetics) overlaps option 2 on every qualifying set and forces a question on each. A gene report alone never raises a tier; IHC and Lab Report ticked without morphology cannot reach this rung because morphology is required.

options.label_head: Reviewed — this is not a mast cell neoplasm, or the diagnosis was revi
options.rationale: Review outcome leading to a non-reportable exit; does not follow from which documents exist.
